description: The figure is a multi-level pie (sunburst) chart representing the distribution of medical-ethics topics and their associated subtopics in the MedEthicsQA benchmark, with 4 main slices in the inner ring. The inner categories are Beneficence (blue, the largest slice at roughly about two-fifths of the circle), Autonomy (green, about one-quarter), Non-Maleficence (purple, about one-fifth), and Justice (orange, the smallest at roughly about one-sixth). Each main slice is subdivided into labeled outer-ring segments: Beneficence includes Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation, Comply with Laws and Regulations, Provide Medical Care to Patients, Continual Learning, Provide Assistance in Emergency, Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues, Respect Life, Dignity of Patients, Give Top Priority to Patient’s Interest in Conflict of Interests, Minimizing Conflicts of Interest, Ethical Research, and Open Discussion and Fair Charging of Fees (all in varying shades of blue); Autonomy includes Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve, Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement, Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives, Keep Confidential of Patient’s Information, Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication, Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice, and Respect the Decision-making of Incompetent Patient (in shades of green); Non-Maleficence includes Prevent Patient from Harm, Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care, Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct, and Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain (in shades of purple); and Justice includes Treat Patients Fairly and Equally, Allocate Medical Sources Fairly, Promote Environmental Sustainability, and Promote the Health of Community and Public Education (in shades of orange). The chart uses direct text labels on slices (no separate legend is shown), does not display numeric percentage annotations, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized beyond color grouping.
